title: The people of the house
hookLine: Muslims pray for the Prophet's family in their prayer

lines: AND ON THE FAMILY OF MUHAMMAD.
cards: Near the end of the ritual prayer, Muslims sit, and the words get quiet and personal. They bear witness. They send blessings on the Prophet.
And then, in the words he taught, the blessing widens: on Muhammad, and on the family of Muhammad.
A grandson in a lane, a daughter at a mill, a boy beside him on the pulpit: all folded into the prayer, said again and again across a day. Today: the people of the house.

teach.b: It starts with a verse. In Pickthall's translation of Surah al-Ahzab: "Lo! Allah and His angels shower blessings on the Prophet. O ye who believe! Ask blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation."
The companions knew how to greet him. They didn't know how to ask blessings. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ka'b ibn Ujrah says they asked the Prophet, peace be upon him, exactly that.

teach.h: HOW? AND ON THE FAMILY OF MUHAMMAD.
teach.b: He taught them a form that begins, in Arabic, Allahumma salli ala Muhammad, wa ala ali Muhammad: O God, send blessings on Muhammad, and on the family of Muhammad, as you sent blessings on Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim.
So the family was in the answer from the start. The phrase ahl al-bayt, the people of the house, comes from the same surah.
Pickthall renders it "O Folk of the Household", in a verse that speaks of God wishing to remove uncleanness from them.

teach.h: WHO IS THE HOUSEHOLD? TWO ANSWERS.
teach.b: Who is the household? Here Muslims answer in different ways. In Sahih Muslim, Aisha tells of a morning the Prophet came out wearing a cloak, drew under it Hasan, Husayn, Fatimah and Ali, and recited that verse.

teach.h: AHL AL-BAYT: THE PEOPLE OF THE HOUSE.
teach.b: Shi'a Muslims hold that these, the people of the cloak, are the household the verse means, with a special and lasting place in guiding the community.

Sunni readings include the people of the cloak and also the Prophet's wives, since the verse sits among words addressed to them, and some widen it to his clan. Both love them. Both say their names with honor.
And in both, the blessing in the prayer never stops at one name. It goes on: and on his family.

how: Muslims say the salawat, the blessing on the Prophet and his family, in the sitting near the end of the ritual prayer, and often at other times when his name is mentioned; in some gatherings it is said aloud together.

o: the household of God, meaning the Kaaba in Mecca
the people of the book, Jews and Christians
the people of the house, the Prophet's household

s: the blessing in the prayer names only the Prophet
the form he taught goes on: and on the family of Muhammad.
the companions asked him how to send blessings on him
Ka'b ibn Ujrah reports it in Bukhari, after the verse told them to ask blessings.
all Muslims agree on exactly who the household is
Shi'a Muslims hold it means the people of the cloak; Sunni readings include the wives too.

games.q: you're a companion. a verse tells you to ask blessings on the Prophet, and you don't know the words. what do you do?
o: just say peace be upon him.
games.why: they asked him, and he taught a form that blesses him and his family: wa ala ali Muhammad.

practice: This ends our days on the family: Fatimah, her hands, Hasan and Husayn, and the house they lived in.
If you pray, say the blessing he taught, slowly, a few times, and let the second half land: Allahumma salli ala Muhammad, wa ala ali Muhammad.
If you don't, let the faces of these days come one by one, a daughter at the mill, a boy on the pulpit, a boy in the lane, and hold one household, remembered with love.
